title: foss-mcp machine-readable public-API definition (per language)
description: The structural contract of config/public_api_definition/<lang>.yaml (O2, REQ-G3-012, G3/TC-676): one committed, schema-validated, reviewable file per language describing that language's oracle rule for what counts as a library's PUBLIC surface - scope roots, excluded directories, visibility (leading-underscore convention and dunder handling), the symbol/member kind model, and (for languages where they apply) inheritance, constructors, indexers, bean properties and overloads. This file is consumed by the oracle's (scripts/release/source_differential.py) own production code AND by test suites on both the oracle and extractor sides, as a ground-truth fixture - it is never imported or read by the extractor's production code (src/foss_mcp/extraction/tree_sitter_engine/*.py); that independence is deliberate (see plans/TC-676.yaml's SCOPE NOTE) so a bug in a shared config cannot corrupt both independent implementations identically. This card starts with Python only; the optional per-language fields below exist so later cards can populate them for other languages without a schema change.

language.description: The language this definition describes, e.g. 'python'. Matches this file's own name under config/public_api_definition/<language>.yaml.

scope_roots.description: Where this language's oracle looks for public symbols: either an array of string globs/path fragments, or the literal string 'module-level' for a language (like Python today) with no sub-package scoping concept of its own.

excluded_dirs.description: Directory-name fragments the oracle's own enumerator skips while walking the library tree (for example 'tests', 'examples'). Zero entries is valid for a language whose enumerator excludes nothing.

visibility.description: The rule the oracle's production code applies to decide whether a bare name is public.

private_prefix.description: The leading-character sequence that marks a name private, e.g. '_'. A name that does not start with this prefix is always public.

dunder_exception.description: How a name that itself starts with the doubled private_prefix and ends the same way (a 'dunder', e.g. '__repr__') is treated: 'all' - every such name is public regardless of the private-prefix rule; 'none' - dunders follow the ordinary private-prefix rule with no exception; or an explicit array of the exact dunder names that are public exceptions (every other dunder stays private).

kind_model.description: The top-level symbol kinds this language's oracle produces, e.g. ['class', 'enum'] for Python today.

member_kinds.description: The member kinds this language's oracle produces within a symbol, e.g. ['method', 'enum_value'] for Python today.

inheritance.description: How this language's oracle resolves inherited members, if it does. Absent or null where a language's oracle does not model this (a one-line comment in the YAML file should say why).

constructors.description: How this language's oracle identifies and shapes constructors, if distinct from an ordinary method. Absent or null where a language's oracle does not model this separately.

indexers.description: How this language's oracle identifies indexer members, if the language has a distinct indexer concept. Absent or null where it does not.

bean_properties.description: How this language's oracle identifies getter/setter accessor-pair properties (e.g. Java bean-style accessors), if it does. Absent or null where it does not.

overloads.description: How this language's oracle groups multiple overloaded signatures under one member name, if it does. Absent or null where it does not.
